units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Had I understood anything of the kind, I should not have been a daily guest in your husband's house.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: At any rate, the fact remains that with myself I took no counsel whatever.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well then, with your nearest relatives--as your duty bade you--with your mother and your two aunts.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, that is true. Those three cast up the account for me. Oh, it's marvellous how clearly they made out that it would be downright madness to refuse such an offer. If mother could only see me now, and know what all that grandeur has come to!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Nobody can be held responsible for the result. This, at least, remains clear: your marriage was in full accordance with law and order.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: At the window.
Oh, that perpetual law and order! I often think that is what does all the mischief in this world of ours.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Mrs. Alving, that is a sinful way of talking.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, I can't help it; I must have done with all this constraint and insincerity. I can endure it no longer. I must work my way out to freedom.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: What do you mean by that?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Drumming on the window frame.
I ought never to have concealed the facts of Alving's life. But at that time I dared not do anything else--I was afraid, partly on my own account. I was such a coward.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: A coward?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: If people had come to know anything, they would have said--"Poor man! with a runaway wife, no wonder he kicks over the traces."
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Such remarks might have been made with a certain show of right.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Looking steadily at him.
If I were what I ought to be, I should go to Oswald and say, "Listen, my boy: your father led a vicious life--"
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Merciful heavens--!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: --and then I should tell him all I have told you--every word of it.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You shock me unspeakably, Mrs. Alving.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes; I know that. I know that very well. I myself am shocked at the idea.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Goes away from the window.
I am such a coward.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You call it "cowardice" to do your plain duty? Have you forgotten that a son ought to love and honour his father and mother?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Do not let us talk in such general terms. Let us ask: Ought Oswald to love and honour Chamberlain Alving?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Is there no voice in your mother's heart that forbids you to destroy your son's ideals?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But what about the truth?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But what about the ideals?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh--ideals, ideals! If only I were not such a coward!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Do not despise ideals, Mrs. Alving; they will avenge themselves cruelly. Take Oswald's case: he, unfortunately, seems to have few enough ideals as it is; but I can see that his father stands before him as an ideal.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, that is true.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And this habit of mind you have yourself implanted and fostered by your letters.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes; in my superstitious awe for duty and the proprieties, I lied to my boy, year after year. Oh, what a coward--what a coward I have been!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You have established a happy illusion in your son's heart, Mrs. Alving; and assuredly you ought not to undervalue it.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: H'm; who knows whether it is so happy after all--? But, at any rate, I will not have any tampering with Regina. He shall not go and wreck the poor girl's life.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No; good God--that would be terrible!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: If I knew he was in earnest, and that it would be for his happiness--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: What? What then?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But it couldn't be; for unfortunately Regina is not the right sort of woman.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, what then? What do you mean?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: If I weren't such a pitiful coward, I should say to him, "Marry her, or make what arrangement you please, only let us have nothing underhand about it."
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Merciful heavens, would you let them marry! Anything so dreadful--! so unheard of--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Do you really mean "unheard of"? Frankly, Pastor Manders, do you suppose that throughout the country there are not plenty of married couples as closely akin as they?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I don't in the least understand you.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh yes, indeed you do.
units.name: MRS. ALVING
